concerns.text: Task T016b modifies `code/data/processed/graphs.parquet` metadata to include a scarcity flag. This violates Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) which states 'No data may be modified in place; every transformation MUST produce a new file with a documented derivation.' The task must be rewritten to write a new file (e. g., `graphs_v2.parquet`) or a separate metadata file, rather than modifying the existing artifact in place.

Task T034 implements an 'unpaired Welch's t-test' to satisfy FR-006. However, Constitution Principle VI (Ligand-Environment Generalization) explicitly mandates 'a statistical comparison (paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank)'. The task silently relaxes a constitutional requirement by switching to an unpaired test without a documented, approved deviation in the spec that overrides the constitution. This is a constitutional violation.

Task T017a performs cutoff sensitivity analysis to select a cutoff minimizing variance. The spec (FR-002) and plan require constructing graphs with edge attributes based on a distance cutoff. The task does not explicitly state that the selected cutoff must be the one used for the *final* graph construction in T017b, creating a risk that the final graphs use a default or hardcoded cutoff, violating the requirement to use the optimized parameter.

Task T036 calculates speed-up factor (SC-004) by running `psi4` on a 'single representative sample'. Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) and Principle IV (Single Source of Truth) require that metrics trace back to data. A single sample is not a statistically robust reference for a 'speed-up factor' of the system. The task must either run on a representative subset or explicitly cite a pre-verified benchmark dataset, rather than generating a potentially misleading single-point metric.
